title: Subject pronouns in sentences
focus: Learn when a olla sentence can omit a subject pronoun and when it should remain explicit.

exercises.prompt: Which shorter sentence still means “I am in Finland tomorrow”?
exercises.explanation: Minä can be omitted here because the ending in olen already identifies the subject in Finnish.

Correct. Minä can be omitted here because the ending in olen already identifies the subject in Finnish.
“Minä olen Suomessa huomenna.” does not fit this subject or construction. Minä can be omitted here because the ending in olen already identifies the subject in Finnish.
“Suomessa huomenna.” does not fit this subject or construction. Minä can be omitted here because the ending in olen already identifies the subject in Finnish.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: present-tense olla + context (the verb ending identifies the subject)

parts.role: verb: links the subject to the context
parts.formation: minä takes the present-tense form olen

parts.role: context: tells the location or state
